narrative.overview:
Aegis is typeset as a preliminary prospectus for a model: white paper, black ink, one serif family, and a single red reserved for the warning that the figures are preliminary and for the places the model failed. Structure comes from the document trade, not the web: double rules open sections, hairlines divide table rows, labels are set in small caps, every chart is a lettered Exhibit with a caption, a Source line and a table view, and a running head carries the chapter list.

Density is that of a reading document. One text column of 66 characters carries the argument; exhibits may run wider than the column but never break out into decorated panels. Nothing floats, glows or rounds off. Depth is made by rule weight alone.

The world rejects the scrolling ML-explainer article: no hero figure, no cards, no shadows, no gradients, no rounded corners, no labels stacked above headings.
keyCharacteristics: White paper (#ffffff), near-black ink (#111111), greys for hierarchy, one red.
Source Serif 4 with optical sizes for everything; lining tabular figures throughout.
A ladder of rule weights (double, heavy, ink hairline, grey hairline) replaces boxes and shadows.
Lettered Exhibits, each with caption, Source line and "View as a table".
Charts drawn twice: a wide drawing and a narrow one, swapped at 600px.

rules.name: The Red Herring Rule
rules.body: Red appears only on the preliminary legend, on misses, and on breaches or rejected models. If a red mark does not signal a warning or a failure, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Ink Band Rule
rules.body: Intervals and ranges are drawn as tinted ink; comparison methods are dashed Caption Ink edges. Data color comes from ink weight, not from a palette.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every word is Source Serif 4; the monospace stack appears only around code inside practitioner notes.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Lining tabular figures are on globally, so every number in prose, tables and charts aligns in columns.

rules.name: The Inline Label Rule
rules.body: Small-caps labels sit inline with or beside what they name ("Exhibit A · title", "Source …", "Risk factors."), never as a separate line stacked above a heading.

rules.name: The Drawn Twice Rule
rules.body: Every chart ships two drawings from the same data: a wide 720-unit viewBox and a narrow 400-unit one with larger relative text and labels moved above rows. They toggle at 600px; a chart is never just scaled down.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing lifts off the page. If an element needs emphasis, give it a heavier rule or more space, not elevation.

rules.name: The Rule Ladder Rule
rules.body: Each rule weight has one meaning; pick the weight by the boundary it marks, never for decoration.

rules.name: The Lettered Exhibit Rule
rules.body: Every chart is a lettered Exhibit with caption, Source line and table view, and carries an accessible label summarising what it shows.

dos: **Do** reserve Herring Red for the legend, misses and breaches or rejected models (The Red Herring Rule).
**Do** open every chapter with a 3px double ink rule and every exhibit with a 2px ink rule.
**Do** letter every chart as an Exhibit with a one-line caption, a Source line and a "View as a table" disclosure.
**Do** draw every chart twice, wide (720) and narrow (400), toggled at 600px.
**Do** keep prose to a 66ch measure and figures tabular.
**Do** draw the method in focus in Ink and the others in Ghost Grey.
donts: **Don't** use cards, panels or background fills to group content; use rules and space.
**Don't** use shadows, gradients or rounded corners.
**Don't** add a second typeface outside code.
**Don't** set a label, kicker or eyebrow on its own line above a heading.
**Don't** use red for emphasis, links, hover, selection or highlight states.
**Don't** scale a wide chart down for phones; ship its narrow drawing.
